mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 70% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% within two months signals a decline in demand for new homes, which is a leading indicator of reduced economic activity and typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of the instances where HOUST decreased by more than 10% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 2% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, signals a stable economic environment that typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 45% of the periods where CPIAUCSL remained below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over a month, it signals strong labor market conditions, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and economic activity are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) both increase by more than 0.5% within a month, it signals a tightening monetary policy coupled with rising inflation, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs and inflationary pressures rise.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% within a month.
